analysis:
Examined both documentation changes, the operations file's base/head and patch, and unchanged surrounding desktop lifecycle/security descriptions. docs/operations/desktop-release.md:64-85 introduces a fixed HTTPS generic GUI update feed, artifact hash/size checks, background downloads and installation on quit, with documented same-Developer-ID verification. Lines 103-106 distinguish stopping propagation from downgrading already-updated clients. docs/developer/desktop-app.md:554-564 requires separate GUI/native update qualification and interrupted-operation reconciliation; lines 604-639 describe installer cancellation, IPC boundaries and native signature verification. No concrete security regression is established by these documentation excerpts; GUI updating is explicitly separate from provider release authorization and does not itself claim App Attest qualification, encryption changes or billing authority.
The new mutable feed and automatic GUI installation expand release-publication authority over installed provider frontends. Relevant canonical contracts include TB-003, T-013, T-043, T-054 and A-017; T-041 cache protections have no observed change here. Integration must verify .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml, desktop-app/scripts/update-feed.mjs and desktop-app/src/main/{updates,updateFeed}.ts against these claims: fixed feed enforcement, runtime signature/identity checks, publication ordering under concurrent releases, and safe quit/update interaction with native operations. Those implementations are outside this supplied source scope, so their absence is not a missing-control finding. Remaining material uncertainty is whether implementation actually enforces the documented update authenticity and lifecycle contracts, and whether the threat model covers the new GUI update authority separately from provider build qualification.
